title: Regional launch corridor simulation and operational rehearsals for rolling model-serving and console feature waves
creator: Ava Nguyen
description: Scope: build and execute a repeatable 'launch corridor' simulation that stitches regional capacity reservations, staggered canaries, and console rollouts for runtime and API changes. Goal is a playbook and automated simulation harness that lets PM/Eng/SRE test phased rollouts (region-by-region + traffic cohorting) against realistic load, latency SLOs, and fallback policies. Deliverables: (1) simulation harness and scenario matrix, (2) documented runbook for pre-launch rehearsals, (3) stakeholder cadence and decision gates for go/no-go, (4) one cross-team dry run and one pressure test before start of Q2 ramp.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation harness can run 5 representative scenarios (cold start, peak burst, kernel-fallback, regional outage, KV-cache regression) and emit per-route latency/cost traces
Runbook includes explicit ownership for each launch step, signal thresholds, and rollback steps and is approved by Eng, SRE, and Console leads
One end-to-end rehearsal executed with >=3 teams (Runtime, Console, API) with captured outcomes and retrospective
Capacity hedging plan defined (reserve slots per region + burst lanes) and entered into Dedicated capacity allocation spreadsheet
Monitoring dashboards and canary health checks are wired into the Console launch page and tested during rehearsal

risks: Accidental coupling of console rollout to runtime version pinning could block fast rollback
Dedicated capacity reservations may incur unexpected cost if hedging lanes are over-provisioned
Observability gaps for some model-serving KPI (KV cache hit-rate by cohort) — may hide regressions
Cross-team scheduling conflicts could delay rehearsals and push the window past Q2 ramp
simulation_plan: Week 1: finalize scenario matrix and traffic profiles; gather historical distributions from Console and Runtime telemetry
Week 2-3: implement synthetic traffic generator and scenario runner; baseline steady-state and burst tests
Week 4: wire simulator outputs to Canary dashboard and validate alerting thresholds
Week 5: run two internal rehearsals (dry-run + pressure test) across regions EU/US/APAC
Week 6: capture results, finalize runbook, and seek stakeholder signoff

2026-04-19: Pressure test (peak burst) — objective: validate capacity hedging and fallbacks
2026-04-26: Final dress rehearsal — objective: validate rollback procedures and dashboard readiness
observability_checks: Per-route p95 and p99 latency tracked alongside token-level cost delta
KV-cache hit-rate by prefix cohort and time-window
Canary health check: end-to-end response verification including structured-output schema checks
Tracing correlation ID propagation between Console -> API -> Runtime
rollback_criteria: Sustained p99 latency above SLO + error-rate spike > 0.5% for 10 minutes
Evidence of quality regression on golden prompt set (automated eval failure rate > 2%)
Telemetry shows capacity exhaustion in the target region with no viable burst lanes
Security anomaly or audit log gap discovered during rehearsal
